title: Modern Systems Programming with Scala Native
note: Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: Whaling teaches systems programming in Scala by compiling to native code with Scala Native, which gives direct access to C’s memory model and the POSIX APIs without a JVM. Part I works at the level of C: raw input and output, pointers, structs and manual heap allocation, a hand-written HTTP client, a minimal shell built on fork and exec, and a blocking TCP server. Part II rebuilds those tools on modern foundations: an event loop on libuv, futures and asynchronous patterns for distributed programs, streaming pipes over files and sockets, an embedded key-value database (LMDB) for durability, and finally composing it all into networked services. An appendix sets up the toolchain on macOS or in Docker.
